description: Sync issues and error events from the Sentry projects you choose, plus the organization's projects, teams and members. Sentry permissions are not carried over.
opening: Sync issues and error events from the Sentry projects you select, plus project, team and member records. Each issue, event, project, team and member is one document. Teams and members cover the whole organization, even when you select only a few projects.

Sentry access controls are not imported, so every synced item is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. An event is not linked to the issue it belongs to. Issue comments, stack traces and breadcrumbs are not synced.

notes: Sentry team-based project access is not reproduced.

connect.auth: Sentry uses an internal integration token.

credentials.name: api_token
credentials.text: The token of a Sentry internal integration, created under Organization settings, Developer settings.

settings.name: organization
settings.text: The organization slug. If you leave it out, HydraDB uses the first organization the token returns, and warns if the token reaches more than one.

connect.permissions_label: Scopes to give the internal integration

steps.title: Create an internal integration
steps.text: In Sentry, open your organization's Developer settings and create an internal integration with `org:read`, `project:read` and `event:read`. Copy its token.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the token as `api_token`. If the token reaches more than one organization, set `organization` to the one you want.

steps.title: Select projects
steps.text: HydraDB lists the projects the token can see, by slug. Listing stops after 20 pages. Select the projects to sync.

connect.account: One connector reads one Sentry organization.

sync.first_sync: Issues and events reach back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default. Issues are measured by when they were last seen, events by when they were created. Selected projects, teams and members are read in full, whatever their age.
sync.changes: Each sync reads issues seen again since the last sync and events created since then. Selected projects, teams and members are read in full on every sync.
sync.edits: An issue is read again when it recurs. A change of status or assignee without a new occurrence may not be picked up.
sync.deletes: Resolving or ignoring an issue changes its status. It does not remove the document. An item deleted in Sentry stays searchable in HydraDB.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: Issues
documents.one_document: One Sentry issue: a group of similar errors.
documents.title: The issue title. An issue with no title is called `Sentry issue` with its id.
documents.text: The title, then a `Culprit` line, the exception type and value, and `File`, `Function`, `Level` and `Project` lines. The status, the assignee and the issue's short id are searchable too.
documents.date: When the issue was last seen, else when it was first seen.

attributes.name: Issue id
attributes.text: The short id, such as `PROJECT-123`, else the numeric id. Keeps later syncs on the same document, and a search can match it.

attributes.name: status
attributes.text: `resolved`, `unresolved` or `ignored`, so a query can match the issue's status.

attributes.name: assignee
attributes.text: The assigned user's or team's name, else their email, written as an `Assignee` line. The graph records the issue as assigned to them.

attributes.name: culprit
attributes.text: The code location Sentry blames, written as the `Culprit` line.

attributes.name: level
attributes.text: The severity, written as the `Level` line.

attributes.name: first_seen, last_seen
attributes.text: When the issue first and last occurred. The last occurrence, else the first, is the result date. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.sentry_id
attributes.text: The numeric issue id. Picks out one issue. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.sentry_short_id
attributes.text: The short id, such as `PROJECT-123`. Picks out one issue. This key is not searchable, but the short id is part of the issue text.

attributes.name: num_comments, user_count
attributes.text: How many comments the issue has and how many users it affected.

attributes.name: logger, platform
attributes.text: The logger and platform that produced the issue.

documents.name: Error events
documents.title: The event title, else its message. An event with neither is called `Sentry event` with its id.
documents.text: The title, then `Message`, `Culprit`, `Location`, `Platform` and `Project` lines. The event id is searchable too.

attributes.name: Event id
attributes.text: The Sentry event id. Keeps later syncs on the same document, and a search can match it.

attributes.name: message, culprit, location, platform
attributes.text: The event message, the blamed code location, the location and the platform, each written as its own line.

attributes.name: project_id, parent_id
attributes.text: The event's project, as `project:<id>`, written in the `Project` and `Parent` lines. Links the event to its project's record.

attributes.name: Event time
attributes.text: When the event was created. Not searchable.

attributes.name: group_id
attributes.text: The id of the issue the event belongs to. It does not link the event to the issue.

documents.name: Projects and teams
documents.title: The name, else the slug. A record with neither gets a generated title with its id.
documents.text: The name and a `Slug` line. A project also has `Platform` and `Status` lines. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the project or team was created.

attributes.name: Project id
attributes.text: A project's id, as `project:<id>`. Events of the project link to this record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Creation time
attributes.text: When the project or team was created. Not searchable.

attributes.name: object_type
attributes.text: `project` or `team`.

documents.name: Members
documents.title: The member's name, else their email. A member with neither gets a generated title with their id.
documents.text: The name, then `Email`, `Role` and `Invite status` lines, and any contact details Sentry reports, such as names, organization, emails, phone numbers, a profile link and the creation and update times. The title is searchable too.
documents.link_back: The member's profile link, when Sentry reports one.

attributes.name: email, emails
attributes.text: The member's primary and other emails. Identify the member as a person in the graph.

attributes.name: display_name, provider_user_id
attributes.text: The member's display name and Sentry user id. Name the member as a person in the graph.

attributes.name: first_name, last_name, job_title, organization_name, organization_id, lifecycle_stage
attributes.text: Names, organization, role and invite status, when reported.

attributes.name: owner, owner_email
attributes.text: The record owner and their email, when reported. The graph records the owner as a person.

attributes.name: phones
attributes.text: Phone numbers, when reported. They do not identify the person in the graph.

attributes.name: url
attributes.text: The profile link, when reported. Also the link back.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the membership was created.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: The last reported update, else the creation time. The graph also records it as when the member was last updated.

example_searches: Which unresolved Sentry issues mention a timeout in the payments project?
Which file and function raise the KeyError issue?

connections: An error event to its project's record.
An event is not linked to its issue, and an issue is not linked to its project.
Stack traces are not read for links to code.
No links to items in other tools.
people: Each organization member, identified by email.
graph.from_text: Issue and event titles, messages, culprits and exception text.

not_synced: Issue comments and activity. Only the comment count is kept.
Stack traces, breadcrumbs and tags beyond the issue summary.
Releases, alerts, performance data and replays.
